atoms.b: The Himalayas are found between the ((++Eurasian Pacific)) and Indian plates and were formed when the two plates collided.

Even today, the Indian plate continues to ((++slide_under jump_on)) the Eurasian plate, so the Himalayas are still growing! 9 out of 10 of the ((++tallest smallest)) mountains in the world are in the Himalayas.

atoms.word: E v e r e s t

feedback.end: Mount Everest is the world’s tallest mountain above sea level, standing at 8,848 metres!

atoms.text: This is Rita! She is going to climb up Everest, and we will help her to carry out some fieldwork as she goes up.

atoms.a: Rita is currently at the base of the mountain. According to the thermometer, what temperature is it?
Rita has now climbed 2,000 metres higher, and the temperature is now -10 °C! What is the difference in temperature since the last time it was measured?

feedback.end: For every 1,000 metres of elevation gain in the Himalayas, the temperature gets 6.5 °C cooler on average.

instruction.text: Nearly there! Drag Rita to the top of Everest to reach the summit.

feedback.end: The top of Everest is extremely cold. Today it is -30 °C, but temperatures can get as low as -60 °C! This makes it very dangerous to climb, although many people like Rita still try.
